note: Every class names a log line this source actually prints and the boot-record state that survives the failure. The markdown document is generated from this file by tests/test_recovery_matrix.py, so the two cannot drift.

classes.title: Power lost during the transaction

symptoms.token: BOOT_STATE WARNING=previous boot stopped during a transaction

classes.record_state: Phase == INTENT (1) with no OUTCOME: the record was written before the first mutation and the sequence never returned.
classes.card_state: Unknown. The selection write, the WPR2 window, or an engine reset may have been applied; the card may still be executing or may be halted with reset released.
classes.machine_state: Unknown. The host may have been mid-DMA; firmware state is whatever it was when power dropped.
steps: Do not warm-reboot: a warm reset can leave a falcon running with host buffers already freed.
Remove power at the wall for 30 s so the card's own firmware state is discarded.
Next boot, read the .LOG file on the removable media for BOOT_STATE lines and for the last stage before the sequence.
Confirm the card enumerates with its stock identity in the read-only diagnostic; do not run a transaction on that boot.
If the diagnostic cannot read configuration space, treat the card as faulty and stop.
proof: BOOT_STATE PRESENT=1 with PHASE=2 (OUTCOME) on a later boot
the read-only diagnostic completes with STABLE=1
a subsequent normal boot reaches Windows with the card present
classes.why_unverified: No hardware run has ever lost power mid-transaction; the software-visible record is exercised on the host only.

classes.title: Firmware did not stop, so its buffers were retained

symptoms.token: firmware did not stop; keeping its DMA buffers until power off

classes.record_state: OUTCOME with a failure Status and Armed == 0: the sequence returned, but the engine may still read the buffers.
classes.card_state: Firmware may still be running. The unlock was not verified and the stock driver must not bind while it is active.
classes.machine_state: The image retains the DMA buffers and the device reference on purpose; freeing them would be a use-after-free from the card's point of view.
steps: Do not start Windows on this boot. The image already refuses to hand over in this state.
Remove power at the wall; the retained buffers die with the boot.
Next boot, check BOOT_STATE PRESENT=1 PHASE=2 STATUS for the recorded failure.
Run the read-only diagnostic only; it does not touch firmware state.
proof: the next boot shows no INTENT record
the diagnostic reads a valid PMC, SS0/SS1 and PROM digest
classes.why_unverified: The simulator shows the image retaining buffers and refusing handover; no card has been observed continuing to DMA.

classes.title: The card refused the function-level reset
classes.record_state: OUTCOME with a failure Status and Armed == 0.
classes.card_state: The permission window is still open: the selectors were written and the reset that closes it did not happen.
classes.machine_state: Bus master is clear and the image keeps the buffers it allocated.
steps: Do not boot into Windows: the stock driver expects a reset GSP and an open permission window is not a state it recovers from.
Power off at the wall, wait, and power on.
Next boot, confirm BOOT_STATE shows the failure and run the read-only diagnostic to confirm the selectors are back to their cold values.
proof: the diagnostic reports the cold selector values, not the unlock value
a later transaction is not attempted automatically

classes.title: The WPR2 window is still open after the reset
classes.record_state: OUTCOME with a busy or error Status.
classes.card_state: FWSEC did not close its window. The stock driver rejects a preexisting WPR2 on this path, so it will not bind.
classes.machine_state: The image stops before any further write and retains its buffers.
steps: Power off at the wall; the window is firmware state and does not survive a cold boot.
Next boot, run the read-only diagnostic and confirm WPR2 reads zero.
If WPR2 is still nonzero after a cold boot, treat the card as faulty.
proof: WPR2 low/high both read zero in the diagnostic
the stock driver binds without a WPR2 complaint
classes.why_unverified: The simulator never leaves WPR2 open; this is a hardware-only failure mode.

classes.title: The vendor driver Stop call never returns
classes.record_state: Phase == INTENT: the record is written before the detach, so a hang inside the vendor callback leaves INTENT behind.
classes.card_state: Whatever the vendor Stop callback was doing. The image has no proof that it is safe to continue.
classes.machine_state: The firmware watchdog is the only thing that ends the hang, and only in a build that arms it (GU_WATCHDOG_SECONDS).
steps: Wait for the machine to reset itself if the bounded build is in use; do not power off during a vendor callback.
If no reset arrives, power off at the wall.
On the next boot, expect the same BOOT_STATE WARNING as a mid-transaction power loss and follow that procedure.
proof: the machine resets without operator action, or powers off cleanly
the next boot reports the INTENT record from the hung boot
classes.why_unverified: No Stop bound has been measured, which is why the timer is opt-in and the AD102/GA102 Stop path is refused.

classes.title: The image refuses this card before writing anything
classes.record_state: No INTENT record is written: the refusal happens before the first mutation, so nothing was in flight.
classes.card_state: Untouched. Zero BAR0 writes, zero FLRs, WPR2 not opened.
classes.machine_state: Windows boots normally, or the diagnostic runs. Nothing to recover.
steps: Read the refusal: it names the compiled profile, the chip, or the observed digest and the reason.
For a stock-profile refusal, this image was built for a different card; use the build that matches, or capture the card's values with the diagnostic.
For a SKU refusal, no register table exists for that chip; the diagnostic still runs and is the way to capture one.
For a reference refusal, capture the digest the log prints and add a reference to a reviewed build.
proof: the diagnostic completes with STABLE=1 and the digest printed
no BOOT_STATE INTENT record exists for the boot
classes.why_unverified: The refusal semantics are simulated; the digests and cold values of real cards are not captured.

classes.title: The staged bundle on the ESP is stale or incomplete
classes.record_state: The install record is a separate NVRAM variable; it names the boot that staged it and the bundle digest.
classes.card_state: Untouched: the install build never prepares or drives the card.
classes.machine_state: Nothing to recover; the next boot either re-stages from removable media or reports the mismatch.
steps: Compare the recorded bundle digest with the pinned version in the image.
Re-run the install build from removable media; it is resumable and does not overwrite a verified file.
If the record reports CORRUPT, delete the variable and re-stage.
proof: ASSET_INSTALL PRESENT=1 with the pinned bundle digest and STATE=CURRENT
a boot without removable media loads the staged bundle
classes.why_unverified: Install and resume are simulated; no ESP has been written by this image.

classes.title: A multi-target sequence stopped between cards
classes.record_state: OUTCOME names the card that was being driven; the steps logged before it name the cards that already completed.
classes.card_state: The completed cards are in their post-transaction state; the next card was never touched.
classes.machine_state: Peers are unchanged, because the coordinator verifies them before and after each card.
steps: Read the SELECTED_GPU_STEP lines in order: COMPLETE for finished cards, then the failing step.
Recovery is per card, using the class that matches the failure, not for the sequence as a whole.
Re-run only after the failing card's class procedure has been followed to its proof.
proof: each card's own class proof holds
the next boot reports no INTENT record
classes.why_unverified: Only one card has ever been driven, and not on hardware; the two-target run in the plan has not happened.
